title: Whole-Expression RT Perturbation Campaign
objective: Replace component ablation tests with lawful aRT deformation tests to test the coherence of the higher-order aRT expression.
primary_question: Do stable closures persist under admissible aRT deformation better than under component-removal controls?

required_controls.M1_simple_ablation: Legacy component removal (e.g., set orientation to 0).
required_controls.M2_aRT_substituted_orientation: Replace orientation with a new, but still admissible, orientation pattern (preserving the aRT structure).
required_controls.M3_aRT_substituted_residue: Replace residue trace with a trace from a different, stable run.
required_controls.M4_random_RT_shuffle: Randomize the binding between member RTs (destroys aRT structure but preserves aggregate values).
required_controls.M5_trace_preserving_deformation: Apply an admissibility-preserving transform to the entire aRT.

expected_outcome: M2, M3, and M5 (which preserve the higher-order aRT rule) will sustain triadic closure significantly better than M1 and M4 (which violate Whole Expression Primacy).
